Platform and operations\n1114\t\n1115\t### 16.1 iOS — the binding platform\n1116\t\n1117\t- **No Web Share Target, ever.** \"Share → screenferry\" cannot exist on iOS.\n1118\t- **No File System Access API.** Output must be `navigator.share({files})`, gated on\n1119\t  `canShare`, fired from a **real touch handler**. iOS ignores programmatic blob-anchor\n1120\t  clicks. **Multi-GB export via `share()` is untested and likely to fail** (§19 Q9).\n1121\t- Inbound: `<input type=file>` with **no `accept`** — forces Files, avoids silent\n1122\t  HEIC→JPEG transcoding.\n1123\t- **Service-worker cache deleted after 7 days** unless installed to Home Screen (D13).\n1124\t- **iPhone cannot go fullscreen** (iPad only); standalone display mode substitutes.\n1125\t- **Wake Lock only in Home Screen web apps, iOS 18.4+.** A `pushState` path change kills a\n1126\t  live stream — routing MUST NOT touch the path during capture.\n1127\t- **No `BarcodeDetector`** — and it is structurally unusable everywhere anyway: the spec's\n1128\t  `DetectedBarcode` has **no byte member**.\n1129\t- **No image-capture extensions** — no `exposureCompensation`, so D14's fix does not apply.\n1130\t- **~1 GB storage quota** (§8.4).\n1131\t\n1132\t### 16.2 Deployment\n1133\t\n1134\tStatic bundle to a static host (Cloudflare Pages or equivalent), built in CI on iad-ci.\n1135\tNo backend, no database, no migration. Rollback is redeploying the previous bundle —\n1136\t**but see §16.3, which is what makes rollback non-trivial.**\n1137\t\n1138\t### 16.3 Version skew — the one operations item that genuinely applies\n1139\t\n1140\tTwo devices each hold an independently-cached copy of the app. A static host that updates,\n1141\ta service worker that caches for offline use, and iOS's 7-day eviction mean **device A can\n1142\tbe running a month-old build while device B loads today's**.\n1143\t\n1144\t| Rule | |\n1145\t|---|---|\n1146\t| **Version fields** | The header's 4-bit nibble is a *fast reject* only; the beacon's 1-byte `wireVersion` is authoritative. The nibble is `wireVersion & 0x0F`, so it **wraps after 16 bumps** — a receiver MUST NOT treat a nibble match as compatibility, only as \"worth parsing the beacon\". |\n1147\t| **Wire compatibility** | The beacon's `wireVersion` gates the wire format. A receiver seeing an unknown version MUST report `E-VERSION` with both versions shown and refuse — **never attempt a partial parse**. |\n1148\t| **What is breaking** | Any change to header layout, beacon layout, PRNG, degree distribution, or fragment semantics. Bump `magic_ver`. |\n1149\t| **What is not** | UI, coaching, profile ladder tuning, dwell, new *optional* beacon fields appended at the end. |\n1150\t| **Stage coexistence** | Stage 1/2/3 modulations are distinguished by the beacon's `flags`, not by `magic_ver` — a Stage-1-only receiver MUST ignore colour tiles rather than fail. |\n1151\t| **Rollback consequence** | Rolling the sender back may strand receivers holding a newer cached build. So a wire-version bump is a **one-way door** and MUST be treated as such: ship it only when the previous version has been deployed long enough to be widely cached — **minimum 30 days**, since iOS evicts uninstalled caches at 7 days and D13-installed apps may lag far longer. |\n1152\t| **Update UX** | The service worker SHOULD prompt for update rather than swapping silently mid-transfer.
